emerging_technology: LLM-based tool-using AI agent that retrieves approved policies and case records, analyzes complaints, proposes routing and drafts replies under employee approval
intended_application: Employee-assisted intake, investigation support, routing/escalation suggestions and response drafting for web-submitted credit-card billing disputes
organization: Hypothetical conservative US retail bank with fragmented complaint records
industry_sector: US retail banking and credit-card servicing; actual jurisdiction-specific rules require separate verification
business_need: Assess whether a complaints-assistance pilot can improve case resolution and operating economics without weakening customer protection
users_stakeholders: Customers, complaints employees, operations managers, risk/compliance, information security and internal audit
capabilities_constraints: Assume no approved tool access to complaint records, incomplete policy version control and no audit-ready integration. Actual technology evidence is unchanged.
risk_consequence_context: Misunderstood disputes, unsupported explanations, missed escalation, privacy exposure, customer frustration and excessive reviewer burden. Employees retain final authority; no autonomous refunds, denials or external messages.
management_question: Should management proceed with the same complaints agent before access, evidence lineage and baseline measurement are ready?
time_horizon: Local material impact is tentatively mid-term 12-36 months because the scenario lacks integration readiness. This is not a forecast of general AI capability or competitive threat.
